references.why: Spurgeon adapts the verse into his own aphorism (paired with 'to the wise nothing is trivial'); Segond's 'Tout est pur pour ceux qui sont purs' does not carry the 'nothing is unclean' form the parallel needs.

Re-tensed and blended paraphrase (KJV Ps 102:17, 'regard the prayer of the destitute') with Spurgeon's 'cry of the humble'; Segond 102:18 = 'Il est attentif à la prière du misérable, Il ne dédaigne pas sa prière'.
Re-personed ('your heart') and Spurgeon's 'bitterness' kept; Segond has 'Le cœur connaît ses propres chagrins'.
Re-personed to the plural hearers (Segond: 'Crie à plein gosier, ne te retiens pas').
Reordered and re-personed as Spurgeon quotes it ('He was dead, but is alive again'); Segond: 'mon fils que voici était mort, et il est revenu à la vie'.
Allusion to KJV 'cattle upon a thousand hills'; Segond reads 'Toutes les bêtes des montagnes par milliers'.
Re-personed: Hosea's 'reçois-nous favorablement' turned by Spurgeon into a promise to the hearer ('receive you graciously').
Re-personed from Segond's 'J’aurai pour eux un amour sincère' ('love you freely').
Re-personed from Segond's 'Nous t’offrirons ... l’hommage de nos lèvres' ('render to Him the calves of your lips').
Segond 'Elles m’environnaient comme des abeilles' (feminine, the nations); Spurgeon applies it to the men around him and repeats it inverted, so re-gendered and expanded.
Segond's singular 'détourne l’oreille pour ne pas écouter la loi' put in the plural by Spurgeon's paraphrase.
Segond's 'Sa prière même est une abomination' put in the plural in Spurgeon's paraphrase.
Blended: Segond's 'Père, pardonne-leur' plus Spurgeon's own words for Christ's intercession.
Condensed from Segond's 'Élie dit sept fois: Retourne' to match Spurgeon's 'Go again seven times'.
Spurgeon's free version ('in an acceptable hour ... in an acceptable time') differs from Segond's 'Au temps de la grâce je t’exaucerai, Et au jour du salut je te secourrai'.
Spurgeon's past tense and 'sins ... iniquities' order differ from Segond's 'J’efface tes transgressions comme un nuage, Et tes péchés comme une nuée'.
Spurgeon quotes the verse without 'on me'; Segond's 'celui qui croit en moi a la vie éternelle' shortened accordingly.
